INITIAL CLOSING BRIEF OF COLTON STOLC
I. INTRODUCTION AND REQUESTED RELIEF
Colton Stolc files this Initial Closing Brief on behalf of himself and in support of the A2 Segment Affected Landowners Coalition. Colton opposes every route that uses Segment A2. He supports Segment A3 and asks the ALJs to choose a filed route that avoids A2 if this project is approved. [Stolc Direct Test. at 4:11-17, 5:1-2, 7:10-12.]
This is not complicated. The property Colton is concerned about is family ranch land. He works full time, helps his stepfather and uncle at the ranch, owns two cows with them, and expects to inherit tracts 3504 and 3505. The ranch is used for beef cattle, shop work, water-line repairs, barn work, dove hunting, and coyote hunting. A2 would cross that property and make normal ranch use harder. [Stolc Direct Test. at 4:6-8, 5:9-18, 6:1-8.]
Colton joins the Coalition request that the Application be denied or deferred if the ALJs find the need record is not enough to approve the project at this time. If a CCN is granted, Colton requests that every A2 route be rejected and that the ALJs recommend Route 705, Route 706, Route 659, Route 836, Route 1245, or another filed route that avoids Segment A2.
II. ARGUMENT
A. Applicants have not shown that A2 has to be used.
Colton does not believe Applicants have proven enough to justify placing this 765-kV line through rural homes and ranches. Even if the ALJs find some project need, that does not prove A2 is necessary. Applicants' witness Ms. Perkins testified that Applicants are good with any of the filed routes, and that route selection should be looked at holistically. [Tr. Vol. 2 at 97:5-23.]
That matters here because Colton is not asking for a brand-new route. Filed routes already exist that use A3 and avoid A2. Joe and Michelle Burnett showed that 942 of the 1,246 route IDs include Segment A2, while only 217 include Segment A3. [Joe & Michelle Burnett Direct Test. at 8:32-34.] That does not make A2 better. It shows the filed route set leaned hard toward A2 from the beginning.
The need evidence also does not make A2 necessary. The record discussed a localized generation deficit and import-path limits, but that still does not explain why Colton's family ranch should be crossed when filed non-A2 routes are available. [Tr. Vol. 3 at 216:6-217:14.]
B. A2 would split up the way Colton uses the ranch.
Colton's concern is practical. Segment A2 would cross the property. The family runs beef cattle there. Colton helps with the ranch, has learned electrical work in the shop, helps with plumbing repairs on water lines, and is learning barn work while the family rebuilds a barn. [Stolc Direct Test. at 5:9-13, 6:1-4.]
A2 would make that kind of use harder. Colton specifically testified that A2 would make it hard to use electric hot wires. He also testified that he may not be able to safely hunt there in the future. [Stolc Direct Test. at 6:5-8.] That is the real problem. A route table may call this one segment, but on the ground it becomes a permanent corridor through family ranch land.
C. A2 would limit future family plans.
Colton also has future plans tied to this land. One day he may build a house there. He would like to have a weekend place there. His sister wants to build a veterinary clinic there. Colton testified that the power line would limit the ability to do either. [Stolc Direct Test. at 6:3-4, 7:1-2.]
This should matter. The Applicants looked at current routing numbers, but rural property is not just what sits on it today. Colton put it plainly in his testimony: rural property is what makes Texas, Texas. Large power lines across new rural areas ruin that when the lines could follow other routes and developed areas. [Stolc Direct Test. at 7:6-9.]
D. A2 would also damage existing solar generation.
A2 creates a separate problem that should not be ignored. During Joe Burnett's cross-examination, he explained that he was aligned with Parties 22, 273, 797, and 798 and was questioning about the A2 area that includes tracts 3502, 3503, 3504, and 3505. [Tr. Vol. 3 at 235:1-7.]
That cross-examination showed a major A2 problem. Mr. Marusak agreed that solar farms are common and expansive near Bell County East Switch. He also agreed that a 1,400-foot crossing through a 200-foot right-of-way would remove more than six acres of solar farm. Applicants then acknowledged they had not calculated the generating capacity that would be permanently removed if A2 is built. [Tr. Vol. 3 at 237:8-239:5.]
That is a serious weakness in the A2 case. Applicants are asking for transmission infrastructure while damaging existing generation infrastructure. Mr. Marusak also testified that A3 was routed around the solar facilities and was later modified to move farther from habitable structures. [Tr. Vol. 3 at 239:6-240:4.] That supports Colton's request to use A3 instead of A2.
E. Filed routes already avoid A2.
Colton's route request follows his direct testimony. He supports any route that uses Segment A3. [Stolc Direct Test. at 5:1-2, 7:10-12.] The ALJs do not need to create a new route to give that relief. The Applicants' Combined Data Table includes filed routes that begin A0-A1-A3-A6-C1 and avoid Segment A2. [Applicants' Combined Data Table, Route Composition for Routes 659, 705, 706, 836, and 1245.]
Route 705 should be considered first for Colton because it is a clean A3 substitute for Route 296. Route 296 begins A0-A1-A2-B1-C2-D11-D12. Route 705 begins A0-A1-A3-A6-C1-D11-D12, then continues through the same D11 path instead of using A2. [Applicants' Combined Data Table, Route Composition for Routes 296 and 705.]
Route 706 is another practical A3 route. Routes 659, 836, and 1245 also avoid A2 and should remain available if the ALJs prefer a different complete filed route. [Applicants' Combined Data Table, Routes 659, 706, 836, and 1245.] The important point for Colton is simple: A2 can be avoided.
III. CONCLUSION AND PRAYER
Colton is not asking for special treatment. He is asking the ALJs not to place a permanent 765-kV line across family ranch land when filed A3 routes are already in the record. A2 would interfere with cattle use, hot-wire fencing, hunting, future residential use, and a possible future veterinary clinic. It would also add to an A2 opening that already creates avoidable solar-generation impacts.
Colton respectfully requests that the ALJs support the A2 Segment Affected Landowners Coalition, deny or defer the Application if the record does not support approval, and, if a CCN is granted, reject every route that uses Segment A2. Colton requests Route 705 first, Route 706 next, and then Route 659, Route 836, Route 1245, or another complete filed route that avoids Segment A2.
Respectfully submitted,
/s/ Colton Stolc
Colton Stolc
405 E. 20th Ave.
Belton, Texas 76513
